verdicts.reason: A pushes the RSVP CTA up into a top-left cluster of tag pills, turning it into just another badge. Its text block is a ragged mix of left-aligned and centred lines, 'Solstice Presents' sits below everything it introduces, and there is a large dead zone above the legal line. B has a coherent two-column layout (text left, phone right) and the tags are grouped, but the CTA is still a small pill, 'Solstice Presents' is still last, the lines are cramped, and a large grey missing-asset box sits in the middle of the left column.

A scatters the tags into separate fragments: TASTINGS floats at top right, ALL AGES sits alone, and FREE ENTRY is tiny and unreadable next to a small RSVP button at the bottom. The legal text and the missing-asset box sit between the copy and the CTA. B keeps the pills together and legible, but it buries the CTA among the tags, the copy alignment is ragged, and 'Solstice Presents' sits at the bottom; it is marginally less fragmented.

A turns the CTA into a tag pill at top left, has jumbled left/centre alignment and puts 'Solstice Presents' last. B is a clean phone-left, text-right banner with a centred text stack and all pills in one row. Its flaws: RSVP is just one pill crammed among the tags, 'Solstice Presents' trails the block, and the missing-asset box is large near the logo.

A is close to unusable. The text block sits partly over the decorative circle with ragged left/centre alignment. TASTINGS, ALL AGES, FREE ENTRY and a tiny RSVP Free are scattered around the phone with no grouping, the legal text floats mid-left, and the grey placeholder is a big focal point. B is still flawed (the CTA is buried among tags and the text alignment is jumbled), but its elements are at least grouped and readable.
